jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Second Opinion
jokes.joke: I got scammed by a guy pretending to be a doctor. He examined me, prescribed something, and charged me forty bucks. I only figured it out when my insurance company called and said, "Sir, no legitimate American doctor would let you leave with both kidneys and your savings."

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Doctor's Orders
jokes.joke: I trust doctors way too much. Any doctor. I went in for a routine checkup, guy I'd never met starts pressing on my stomach going 'does this hurt?' and I said 'a little' and he said 'good, means it's working,' and I just nodded like that was a sentence. He could've said 'we're removing your soul, insurance covers half,' and I'd have said thank you and asked if I could drive myself home.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Day Trading Dad
jokes.joke: My brother quit his job to become a full-time stock market day trader, which basically means he loses three thousand dollars before noon and then aggressively mows the lawn so my mom thinks he had a productive day. Yesterday he bought fifty shares of a biotech startup, panicked, and turned our entire backyard into a putting green.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Too Trusting
jokes.joke: I'm way too trusting. Some guy texts me out of the blue: congrats, you've won a free cruise, just cover the small admin fee. I send the money. Three days later it hits me - the only destination I'm booked for is a one-way trip to being scammed.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Backyard Tips
jokes.joke: I tried hiring this guy who said he was a former stock trader to help me fix my backyard. He kept pointing at random patches of dirt saying, "Huge growth potential right here." I trusted him - big mistake. Two weeks later I realized I'd basically paid him to bury my own money... and the dirt still looks bearish.
